title.narrative: UNDP Community resilience and reintegration Al-Hol
UNDP Community resilience and reintegration Al-Hol

description.narrative:
The overall objective of CRRISA II is to support the Government of Iraq in addressing critical migration challenges by focusing on the social and economic reintegration of Iraqi families returning from Al-Hol, while strengthening national and local institutional capacities for migration and reintegration management.
Indicative Output(s):
Output 1: An enabling environment for the return and reintegration of Iraqi nationals from Al Hol camp in NES is created
Output 2: Iraqi returnees from Al-Hol Camp in NES and host communities in areas of return have improved access to socio-economic reintegration opportunities

Projektet "The Road Back Home: Community Reconciliaton and Reintegration of Iraqis Returning from Syria's Al Hol Camp II" syftar till att stödja rehabiliterings- och återintegreringsprocesser för ett hållbart återvändande av irakiska medborgare från Al-Hol lägret i nordöstra Syrien. Insatsen ska bidra till att stödja Iraks regering i arbetet med att hantera centrala migrationsutmaningar, genom att prioritera den sociala och ekonomiska återintegreringen av irakiska familjer som återvänder från Al-Hol. Samtidigt ska nationella och lokala institutioners kapacitet för hantering av återintegrering stärkas. För att säkerställa konfliktsensitivitet och stärkt social sammanhållning riktas insatserna till både återvändande familjer och konfliktdrabbade individer i värdsamhällena.

The project “The Road Back Home: Community Reconciliation and Reintegration of Iraqis Returning from Syria’s Al-Hol Camp II” aims to support rehabilitation and reintegration processes to enable sustainable return of Iraqi citizens returning from the Al-Hol camp in north east Syria. The intervention seeks to support the Government of Iraq in addressing key migration challenges by prioritizing the social and economic reintegration of Iraqi families returning from Al-Hol. At the same time, the capacity of national and local institutions to manage reintegration processes will be strengthened. To ensure conflict sensitivity and promote social cohesion, the interventions target both returning families and conflict-affected individuals in host communities.
